name: Bearded Vulture
body:
Bearded Vulture
CR 1/2

This largish bird has fluffy, pale gold feathers on its head and neck with black feathers sweeping down alongside its beak in a beard-like fringe. Its wings are feathered brown and its long, hooked beak is caked with carrion.

XP 200
N Medium animal
Init +2; Senses carrion scent, low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 12, flat-footed 11 (+2 Dex, +1 natural)
hp 7 (1d8+3)
Fort +7, Ref +4, Will +2; +4 vs. disease

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., fly 50 ft. (average)
Melee bite +2 (1d6+1)
Special Attacks bone-crushing beak

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 7
Base Atk +0; CMB +2; CMD 14
Feats Great Fortitude, Weapon Finesseb
Skills Fly +7, Perception +10; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bone-Crushing Beak (Ex)

When a bearded vulture confirms a critical hit with its beak against a Medium or smaller creature, the target takes 2 points of Strength damage and 2 points of Dexterity damage (DC 13 Fort half), and until this ability damage is healed the target’s speed is also reduced by 10 feet (minimum 5 feet) due to damage to its bones. Skeletal undead can be harmed by this ability. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Carrion Scent (Ex)

A bearded vulture’s scent ability allows it to sense the presence of creatures at 0 hit points or that are taking bleed damage at five times the normal range.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm mountains
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure incidental

Also called a lammergeier or ossifrage, this great bird is not bald like other vultures but is growned with golden head feathers and has a beard of black feathers cascading down from its face. Though related to raptors and other birds of prey, bearded vultures mainly feed on carrion they spot or scent from on high. Vultures have weak claws compared to predatory birds, but their sharp and wickedly hooked beaks tear living flesh as readily as the sharpest blade. The bearded vulture crushes and devours the bones of its prey as readily as their flesh, and in some cases their diet may be mostly bones when meat is scarce. Despite dining on carrion, bearded vultures prefer their corpses newly dead rather than rotten.

Some even hunt smaller prey when food is scarce.
